info.title: TradingAPI supplement
info.description: Supplementary TradingAPI operations maintained in this repository until they are available in the upstream source.

OrderPageBidSize.description: One price band in the tick-size table and its minimum price increment. When a price is greater than `str_proceed` and not greater than `end_proceed`, use this band's `bid_size`.

bid_size.description: Minimum price increment in this band, for example "0.01"

OrderPageOrderTypeConfig.description: Trading sessions and time-in-force values supported by one order type

support_sessions.description:
Trading sessions supported by this order type:
- `1` - Regular trading hours only
- `2` - Regular trading hours plus pre-market and after-hours
- `3` - Overnight session only
- `4` - Pre-market (used for overnight options trading)

An empty list means the order type has no session option, and the order page should hide session selection.

support_time_in_forces.description:
Time-in-force values supported by this order type:
- `0` - Day (DAY)
- `1` - Good till canceled (GTC)
- `3` - Immediate or cancel (IOC)
- `5` - Fill or kill (FOK)
- `6` - Good till date (GTD)

OrderPageGrantedStatus.description: Authorization status of one trading qualification, certification, or risk statement

status.description:
Certification status:
- `0` - Unknown
- `1` - Passed
- `2` - Not passed
- `3` - Pending review

expired.description: Whether the authorization or certification has expired. If it has, the user must complete it again.

url.description: URL of the page where the user completes this authorization or certification

OrderPageChannelInfo.description: Trading configuration of the current account for this security. In addition to the fields below, the response contains several `*_granted` booleans (whether the corresponding authorization, certification, or risk statement is complete) with matching certification URL fields (`*_url`, `*_granted_url`). Some apply only to specific markets or businesses, and the server determines which fields are present. When a value is `false`, guide the user to the matching URL before submitting the order, and call this endpoint again afterward to refresh the status.

account_channel.description: Account channel. Together with `org_id` and `aaid`, it identifies the account this configuration belongs to.

currency.description: Quote currency of the security, for example USD, HKD, or GBX

settlement_currency.description: Available settlement currencies. The first item is the default trading currency; pass it as `currency` when you query positions and cash, buying power, and estimated fees.

order_type_config.description: Order type configuration available for this security and account. Keys are order type codes, for example `LO` (limit order), `ELO` (enhanced limit order), `MO` (market order), `LIT` (limit-if-touched), and `MIT` (market-if-touched). An order type that does not appear is unavailable. When this object is returned, use the per-order-type configuration for sessions and time in force.

support_trade.description: Whether the current account channel supports trading. When `false`, do not offer order entry.

restricted.description:
Online trading restriction:
- `1` - Online buying is not allowed
- `2` - Online selling is not allowed
- `3` - Neither online buying nor online selling is allowed

If the field is absent or has another value, no such restriction applies. For a restricted direction, direct the user to contact the Broker offline.

support_rth.description: Whether pre-market and after-hours trading is supported. When `order_type_config` is returned, `support_sessions` in it takes precedence.

support_overnight.description: Whether overnight trading is supported. When `order_type_config` is returned, `support_sessions` in it takes precedence.

gtd_support_order_types.description: Order type codes that support good-till-date (GTD) orders

support_attached_order_types.description: Order type codes that accept attached orders

support_fractional_shares.description: Whether US fractional-share trading is supported

fractional_min_amount.description: Minimum amount, in USD, for a fractional-share order placed by amount. Orders below this amount are rejected.

mo_avail_ratio.description: Buying-power factor for market orders. Available buying power for a market order (including an untriggered market conditional order) equals `buy_limit` from Get Buying Power for Order Entry multiplied by this factor. Treat an empty value as 1.

finance_account_status.description:
Margin credit status:
- `0` - Normal
- `1` - Credit limit is 0 and an adjustment request is under review
- `2` - Credit limit is 0 and no request is under review

When the value is `1` or `2`, trades that require margin credit, such as opening a short stock position or selling to open options, cannot proceed. Tell the user to wait for review or request a limit adjustment.

account_risk_level.description:
Account risk level:
- `0` - No additional statement is required
- `1` - The user must confirm the trade-anyway statement before ordering
- `2` - The user must confirm the important notice before ordering

confirm_purchase_statement.description: Whether the user has confirmed the trade-anyway statement

confirm_important_notice.description: Whether the user has confirmed the important notice

granted_info.description: Authorization status of each trading qualification and risk statement. Keys are qualification type codes, for example `us_overnight_risk_agreement` (US overnight trading risk statement) and `fractional_shares_risk_agreement` (fractional-share trading risk statement). The server determines the other keys.

OrderPageStockContract.description: Option contract information, returned only for options

contract_direction.description: Option type: `C` for a call, `P` for a put

underlying_counter_id.description: Security ID of the underlying stock

nearing_expire.description: Whether the option is close to expiry

contract_model.description:
Option margin mode:
- `1` - Non-margin mode
- `2` - Margin mode

open_purchase_limit.description: Minimum buying power required to open an option position. No threshold applies when `threshold` is empty or 0.

OrderPageTradableButton.description: Guidance button in the tradability dialog

type.description:
Action on tap:
- `0` - Close the dialog without entering order entry
- `1` - Open the order page for this security
- `2` - Open the page that `link` points to

direction.description:
Order direction when `type` is `1`:
- `0` - Not restricted
- `1` - Buy only
- `2` - Sell only

TradeAuthToken.description: Trade token and its refresh token, issued per account

token.description: Trade token. Pass it as `tradeToken` to `WhaleCoreService.updateTradeToken(...)`

refresh_token.description: Refresh token. Pass it as `tradeRefreshToken` to `updateTradeToken`; it is also the input of `POST /v1/member/trade/refresh_token`

refresh_token_expires.description: Lifetime of the refresh token, in seconds, counted from issuance

SearchSecurityItem.description: A single security candidate in search results

counter_id.description: Security ID in the format `<product>/<market>/<code>`, such as `ST/US/AAPL`. Use it to identify the security in follow-up actions such as opening the security detail page or adding it to a watchlist

code.description: Security code, such as `AAPL` or `700`. Pass it as the `code` parameter when you load the next page

name.description: Security name in the request language

market.description: Market of the security, such as `HK` or `US`. Broker App uses it to display the market badge

currency.description: Trading currency, such as `USD` or `HKD`. For fund results, Broker App displays the currency instead of the market badge

product.description: Security product code, such as `ST`, `ETF`, or `UT`

score.description: Ranking score of the result. To load the next page, pass the value from the last result of the previous page as the `score` parameter

tx_type.description: Record type code, such as `cash_in` or `cash_out`. Use `type_name` for Client-facing display

type_name.description: Localized record type name in the request language. Broker App displays it as the record title

category.description: Direction prefix for the amount. Broker App prepends it to `amount` as is; when it is empty, only the amount is displayed

amount.description: Cash change amount as a decimal string. An empty value or `0` means the record only involves a change in share quantity

currency.description: Currency of the amount, such as `HKD` or `USD`

stock_quantity.description: Change in share quantity. When it is not empty, `quantity_description` provides the Client-facing text

quantity_description.description: Localized description of the share quantity change. Broker App shows it as the main value when the record only changes shares, and as secondary text when an amount is also present

description.description: Localized supplementary text for the record. Broker App shows it after the date when it is not empty

created_at.description: Record creation time as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Broker App groups the list by the year and month of this time

done_at.description: Record completion time as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Broker App displays this date in the list

WithdrawRecordState.description:
Withdrawal request status:
- `0` - Submitted and being processed
- `1` - Processing
- `2` - Rejected
- `3` - Cancelled by the Client
- `4` - Remitted
- `5` - Failed
- `6` - Refunded
- `7` - Approved but not yet remitted
- `8` - Under large-amount withdrawal review
- `9` - Modification pending approval
- `10` - Deletion pending approval
- `11` - Deleted
- `12` - Rejection pending approval
- `15` - To be confirmed: the Client must confirm a change of the receiving bank card before processing continues

Only requests in status `0` or `15` can be cancelled. When displaying the status, prefer the returned `state_description`.

WithdrawPayeeAddress.description: Payee address of a bank card

payee_country.description: Payee country or region as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code (for example, `HKG`), taken from `code2` of “Get Payee Countries and Regions”

payee_building.description: Building name; required only for some countries or regions

id.description: Bank card id, used as `card_id` for the pre-check and the withdrawal request

bank_card_identity.description: Bank card identity. Together with `id`, it identifies one bank card; pass it with `card_id` when submitting a withdrawal request

bank_code.description: Bank code; `FPS` indicates a Faster Payment System (FPS) receiving account

account_type.description: Currency the card supports for withdrawals, for example `HKD`; `ALL` means all currencies. The withdrawal currency must match this value unless it is `ALL`

region.description: Full name of the region where the bank card is issued, for example `HONGKONG`

status.description:
Bank card verification status:
- `0` - Not verified; the card must be verified first
- `1` - Under verification review; withdrawals cannot be submitted
- `2` - Verified

witness_state.description:
Deposit witness status:
- `1` - No witness required
- `2` - Witness pending
- `3` - Witnessed

For accounts opened with cash verification, only cards in status `1` or `3` can be used for withdrawals.

bind_state.description:
Binding status:
- `0` - Binding under review
- `1` - Bound
- `2` - Binding failed

Treat a missing value as bound. Only bound cards can be used for withdrawals.

get.description:
Retrieves the order rules and configuration for a security under the current account when the user opens the order page, switches securities, or switches accounts: lot size, tick-size table, order price limits, order tag, the trading sessions and time-in-force values supported by each order type, support for good-till-date and attached orders, US fractional shares, available settlement currencies, online buy and sell restrictions, the market order buying-power factor, and the status of authorizations and statements required before ordering. A Broker-built order page uses this response to determine the available order types, sessions, time in force, quantity step, and price step, and to block submission when an authorization is missing. When amending an order, pass the original order ID to get the configuration for that order. After the user completes an authorization or certification, call this endpoint again to refresh the status. This endpoint is also used by the recurring investment plan creation page (to read the trading configuration of the security) and by the options income and protection strategy pages (to read the authorization status of the strategy risk agreement).

WhaleCore's `orderService()` wraps this endpoint as the typed method `getOrderInfo`. If you use WhaleCore, prefer that method.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), for example `ST/US/AAPL` or `ST/HK/700`

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Original order ID when amending an order. Omit it for a new order.

parameters.name: order_id_str
parameters.description: String form of the original order ID. When amending an order, pass the same value as `order_id`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Order Configuration” operation.

last_done.description: Latest price in the quote currency

lot_size.description: Lot size. Use it as the quantity step when `buy_lot_size` or `sell_lot_size` is empty.

upper_limit.description: Upper price limit. The order price cannot exceed this value.

lower_limit.description: Lower price limit. The order price cannot be below this value.

tag.description:
Order tag. Pass it as `order_tag` when estimating trading fees:
- `1` - Regular order
- `2` - Long-term order
- `3` - Grey market order

timestamp.description: Current server time as a Unix timestamp in seconds

bid_sizes.description: Tick-size table used to determine the minimum price increment for a price and to validate or adjust the order price. When no band matches, use the first item.

is_connect.description: Whether the security is traded through China Connect

is_spac.description: Whether the security is a SPAC

is_rights.description: Whether the security is a rights issue

get.description:
Checks whether a security can be traded in the current account when the user switches or searches for a security on the order page, and returns a prompt and guidance buttons. When `is_alert` is `true`, show `msg` and `buttons` in a dialog instead of opening order entry directly; if `buttons` is empty, treat the security as not tradable. When `is_alert` is `false`, the order page can open; if `is_toast` is also `true`, show `msg` as a brief toast.

WhaleCore's `orderService()` wraps this endpoint as the typed method `checkTradability`. If you use WhaleCore, prefer that method.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), for example `ST/US/AAPL` or `ST/HK/700`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Check Security Tradability” operation.

is_cnconnect.description: Whether the security is traded through China Connect

is_alert.description: Whether to show a dialog and block direct order entry

is_toast.description: When order entry is allowed, whether to show `msg` as a toast

support_regular_saving_plan.description: Whether the security supports recurring investment plans

get.description: Checks, when the order page loads, whether a day (DAY) order for this security submitted now would roll to the next trading day. When the result is `true`, you can show "Valid until the close of the next trading day" next to the time in force on the order confirmation page. The result applies only to day orders: read `is_next_day` when the order trades during regular hours only, and `is_next_day_after` when it also trades pre-market and after-hours. A limit order for the overnight session only follows the overnight session rules and does not use this result.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), for example `ST/US/AAPL` or `ST/HK/700`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Check Next-Trading-Day Rollover” operation.

is_next_day.description: Whether a day order that trades during regular hours only rolls to the next trading day

is_next_day_after.description: Whether a day order that also trades pre-market and after-hours rolls to the next trading day

get.summary: Get Position and Cash for Order Entry
get.description:
Retrieves, when the order page loads, the position quantity, available quantity, and cost of the current account in a security, together with the cash in the specified currency, to show the position and the quantity available to sell. The returned `quantity`, `average_cost`, and `diluted_avg_cost` are inputs to Estimate Post-Trade Average Cost, and the sign of `quantity` determines `position_side` when estimating trading fees. When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

WhaleCore's `orderService()` wraps this endpoint as the typed method `getTradeDetail`. If you use WhaleCore, prefer that method.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), for example `ST/US/AAPL` or `ST/HK/700`

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Trading (settlement) currency, for example USD or HKD. Use the first item of `channel_infos.settlement_currency` returned by Get Order Configuration.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Position and Cash for Order Entry” operation.

quantity.description: Position quantity. A negative value indicates a short position.

underlying_available_quantity.description: For an option, the available position quantity of the underlying stock

get.description: Retrieves, on a stock (non-option) order page that already holds a trade token, the initial margin factors of the current account for opening long and short positions in the stock. Use them to estimate locally the tradable quantity and the required margin for a margin buy or a short sale: use `long_im_factor` to open by buying and `short_im_factor` to open by selling. Option orders do not use this endpoint. When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), for example `ST/US/AAPL` or `ST/HK/700`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Stock Initial Margin Factors” operation.

long_im_factor.description: Initial margin factor for opening a long position, for example "0.5"

short_im_factor.description: Initial margin factor for opening a short position

get.summary: Get Buying Power for Order Entry
get.description: Retrieves the maximum buying power of the current account for a security when the order page loads or the user switches accounts or settlement currencies, to show the amount available to buy and to validate the order amount. For a market order (including an untriggered market conditional order), available buying power equals `buy_limit` multiplied by `channel_infos.mo_avail_ratio` from Get Order Configuration. When amending an order, pass the original order ID; omit `order_id` when the order being amended is an untriggered conditional order. When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), for example `ST/US/AAPL` or `ST/HK/700`

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Trading (settlement) currency, for example USD or HKD. Use the first item of `channel_infos.settlement_currency` returned by Get Order Configuration.

parameters.name: account_channel
parameters.description: Broker channel

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Original order ID when amending an order. Omit it for a new order or when amending an untriggered conditional order.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Buying Power for Order Entry” operation.

get.description:
Estimates the commission, third-party charges, and platform fee of a trade from the security, order price, quantity, and direction after the user changes the price or quantity on the order page, to show the estimated fees. The sum of the three can be passed as `fee_amount` to Estimate Post-Trade Average Cost. Do not call this endpoint when the price or quantity is 0. When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

WhaleCore's `orderService()` wraps this endpoint as the typed method `getEstimatedCost`. If you use WhaleCore, prefer that method.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), for example `ST/US/AAPL` or `ST/HK/700`

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Trading (settlement) currency, for example USD or HKD. Use the first item of `channel_infos.settlement_currency` returned by Get Order Configuration.

parameters.name: price
parameters.description: Order unit price in the trading currency. For a UK security quoted in GBX and traded in GBP, divide by 100 to convert to GBP first.

parameters.name: qty
parameters.description: Order quantity in shares

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description:
Order direction:
- `0` - Buy
- `1` - Sell

parameters.name: account_channel
parameters.description: Broker channel

parameters.name: order_tag
parameters.description:
Order tag. Use `tag` from Get Order Configuration:
- `1` - Regular order
- `2` - Long-term order
- `3` - Grey market order

parameters.name: order_type
parameters.description: Order type code, for example `LO` or `MO`

parameters.name: position_side
parameters.description: Position side. Pass `LONG` when the current position is greater than 0 and `SHORT` when it is less than 0. With no position, pass `LONG` to buy and `SHORT` to sell.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Estimate Trading Fees” operation.

get.description: Calculates the average purchase cost and the diluted cost after the trade from the current position quantity and cost and the order price and quantity. Call it after Estimate Trading Fees succeeds, and show the result as the estimated cost on the order page. To include trading fees in the cost, pass `fee_amount`. When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), for example `ST/US/AAPL` or `ST/HK/700`

parameters.name: holding_quantity
parameters.description: Current position quantity. Use `quantity` from Get Position and Cash for Order Entry.

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: Order direction

parameters.name: avg_cost
parameters.description: Current average purchase cost. Use `average_cost`; pass `0` when there is no position.

parameters.name: diluted_avg_cost
parameters.description: Current diluted cost. Use `diluted_avg_cost`; pass `0` when there is no position.

parameters.name: price
parameters.description: Order unit price, the same as `price` passed to Estimate Trading Fees

parameters.name: quantity
parameters.description: Order quantity in shares

parameters.name: fee_amount
parameters.description: Trading fees to include in the cost: the sum of `commission`, `third`, and `platform` from Estimate Trading Fees. When omitted, the cost excludes fees.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Estimate Post-Trade Average Cost” operation.

avg_cost.description: Average purchase cost after the trade

post.description:
Verifies the trade password entered by the Client. If verification succeeds and no second-factor verification is required, returns the trade token for the account.

WhaleCore handles trade authentication automatically by default, so the host app does not need this operation. When WhaleCore is initialized with `tradePasswordEnabled: true`, the SDK no longer obtains trade tokens itself. When a trading call throws `tradeAuthFailed` (1006) or `hasTradeToken()` returns `false`, the host app asks the Client for the trade password, calls this operation, passes `data.token.token` as `tradeToken` and `data.token.refresh_token` as `tradeRefreshToken` to `WhaleCoreService.updateTradeToken(...)`, and then retries the original operation. Tokens are issued per account, so the `accountChannel` passed to `updateTradeToken` must match the account of this request.

If `need_two_factors` or `need_totp_two_factors` is `true`, do not use any token in this response. Call the matching second-factor operation instead, which returns the token: `POST /v1/member/trade/auth_two_factors` for an SMS verification code, or `POST /v1/member/trade/totp/auth_two_factors` for a third-party authenticator code. Device-token verification, indicated by `need_device_totp_two_factors`, is outside the scope of this document.

This operation is also used to verify the Client’s current trade password before security settings are changed.

If the password is wrong, show `message` and let the Client enter it again. If 402009 is returned, stop retrying.

Password fields carry the MD5 digest of the 6-digit trade password as a 32-character lowercase hexadecimal string. Never send the plaintext password.

This operation obtains the trade token, so do not set `requiresTradeToken` to `true` when you call it through WhaleCore `requestService()`.

trade_password.description: MD5 digest of the trade password

type.description: Verification scenario. Pass `trade` to unlock trading.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Verify Trade Password” operation.

need_two_factors.description: Whether SMS second-factor verification is still required. If `true`, call `POST /v1/member/trade/auth_two_factors`

need_totp_two_factors.description: Whether third-party authenticator (TOTP) second-factor verification is still required. If `true`, call `POST /v1/member/trade/totp/auth_two_factors`

need_device_totp_two_factors.description: Whether device-token second-factor verification is still required. This verification method is outside the scope of this document

tfa_guide.description: If `true`, the SMS second-factor page can offer an option to require the verification code for this unlock only. Submit the choice through `tfa_switch` of `POST /v1/member/trade/auth_two_factors`

token.description: Trade token. Use it only when none of the three `need_*` fields is `true`

400.description: The service rejected the request because a business rule or input validation failed. Review the business codes and correct the request before retrying.

x-business-codes.description: The trade password retry limit has been reached and trade unlock for the account is frozen. Show `message` and do not retry

post.summary: Submit SMS Verification for Trade Unlock
post.description:
Completes SMS second-factor verification for trade unlock. After Verify Trade Password returns `need_two_factors: true`, send a trade-unlock SMS verification code to the Client (the send-code operation is outside the scope of this document), and then submit the code with the same trade password. On success, returns the trade token: `data.token.token` maps to `tradeToken` and `data.token.refresh_token` maps to `tradeRefreshToken` of `updateTradeToken`.

If `tfa_switch` is provided, this call also changes whether later trade unlocks for the Client require an SMS verification code. If verification fails, show `message` and let the Client re-enter the code or request a new one.

Password fields carry the MD5 digest of the 6-digit trade password as a 32-character lowercase hexadecimal string. Never send the plaintext password.

This operation obtains the trade token, so do not set `requiresTradeToken` to `true` when you call it through WhaleCore `requestService()`.

code.description: SMS verification code received by the Client

trade_password.description: MD5 digest of the trade password, identical to the value submitted to Verify Trade Password

tfa_switch.description:
Changes the SMS verification requirement for later trade unlocks. Omit it to keep the current setting. Offer this choice only when Verify Trade Password returns `tfa_guide: true`:

- `close` - Require SMS verification for this unlock only; later trade unlocks no longer require an SMS code
- `open` - Later trade unlocks continue to require an SMS code

verify_credentials.description: Verification credential returned after the SMS code is checked. Pass it when the code has already been checked separately

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit SMS Verification for Trade Unlock” operation.

token.description: Trade token issued after successful verification

post.summary: Submit Authenticator Code for Trade Unlock
post.description:
Completes second-factor verification for trade unlock with a code generated by the third-party authenticator (TOTP) app bound by the Client. Call it for the same account after Verify Trade Password returns `need_totp_two_factors: true`. The request does not carry the trade password. On success, returns the trade token: `data.token.token` maps to `tradeToken` and `data.token.refresh_token` maps to `tradeRefreshToken` of `updateTradeToken`.

If the code is wrong or expired, show `message` and let the Client enter a new code.

This operation obtains the trade token, so do not set `requiresTradeToken` to `true` when you call it through WhaleCore `requestService()`.

verify_code.description: Current 6-digit code shown in the authenticator app

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit Authenticator Code for Trade Unlock” operation.

token.description: Trade token issued after successful verification

get.description:
Checks whether the trade token carried by the request is still accepted by the server and returns its remaining lifetime. `hasTradeToken()` only reflects whether a token is held locally, so you can call this operation before opening a trading page to confirm that the server still accepts the token and avoid interrupting the Client after the order form is filled in.

Handle an invalid token by business code: 402000 means the token has expired and can be renewed with the refresh token; 402001 means the token has been invalidated, for example because the account signed in on another device, and the trade password must be verified again.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Check Trade Token” operation.

token_expires.description: Remaining lifetime of the trade token, in seconds. If little time remains, refresh the token first

400.description: The service rejected the request because a business rule or input validation failed. Review the business codes and correct the request before retrying.

x-business-codes.description: The trade token has expired. Renew it with `POST /v1/member/trade/refresh_token`; if renewal fails, verify the trade password again
The trade token has been invalidated, for example because the account signed in on another device. Verify the trade password again

post.description:
Exchanges a refresh token for a new trade token and refresh token to extend the trade unlock period. The account is determined by the refresh token itself.

After tokens are passed in through `updateTradeToken`, WhaleCore renews them automatically with `tradeRefreshToken`, so the host app usually does not need this operation. If the host app refreshes tokens itself, pass the returned `data.token.token` and `data.token.refresh_token` to `updateTradeToken` again so that the tokens held by the SDK match the server. A 402003 response means the refresh token has expired and the trade password must be verified again.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Refresh Trade Token” operation.

token.description: New trade token and refresh token

get.description:
Queries the bank cards the Client has bound, together with the bank card and currency used for the last withdrawal. Used on the withdrawal page to select the receiving bank card and to set the default card and currency.

This is the first step of the withdrawal flow. After selecting a card, call “Get withdrawal pre-check information” (`GET /v3/portfolio/withdraw/pre`; some tenant channels use `GET /v4/portfolio/withdraw/pre`) for the withdrawable amount and fees, then call `POST /v5/portfolio/withdraw` to submit the withdrawal. Only cards whose `bind_state` is `1` (or absent), whose `status` is not `1`, and whose `account_type` matches the withdrawal currency can be used. When changing the receiving card of a withdrawal request, also pick the new card from this list.

With `withdraw=0`, it returns all bound bank cards; the endpoint is also used by the bank card management page and for selecting bank cards in ACH and wire deposits and withdrawals.

A complete withdrawal flow runs in this order: get the withdrawal bank cards (`GET /v3/portfolio/withdraw/cards`) → get the withdrawal pre-check information and withdrawable amount (`GET /v3/portfolio/withdraw/pre`; some tenant channels use `GET /v4/portfolio/withdraw/pre`; to get only the withdrawable balance by currency, call `GET /v1/rms_gateway/get_account_all_single_currency_withdraw`) → check and add the payee address when required → submit the withdrawal request (`POST /v5/portfolio/withdraw`) → query withdrawal records and details → cancel the withdrawal or change the receiving bank card when needed.

- `0` - Return all bound bank cards (bank card management, ACH and wire deposits and withdrawals)

get.description:
After the withdrawal currency and receiving bank card are selected, queries the withdrawable limits and withdrawal configuration. It returns the maximum withdrawable amount, the cash amount, the money market fund (MMF) amount, the per-currency breakdown, estimated arrival times, fee tiers by amount range, the available payout methods, and whether withdrawing this currency to this card requires a payee address. Used for the amount display, validation, and fee notices on the withdrawal form. Without `card_id`, it can be used to get card-independent information such as the available payout methods.

General tenant channels use this endpoint; some tenant channels (including southbound and northbound withdrawal scenarios) use `GET /v4/portfolio/withdraw/pre` instead, and the two return largely the same structure. Call it after “Get Withdrawal Bank Cards”. When `need_payee_address` is `true`, call `POST /v1/portfolio/withdraw/card/addresscheck` first, then call `POST /v5/portfolio/withdraw` to submit the withdrawal.

The endpoint is also used for cross-broker fund transfers, where `cash_amount` is the upper limit of the transferable amount.

When calling through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

post.description:
Submits a withdrawal request with the selected currency, amount, and receiving bank card, and returns the withdrawal request id once accepted. `ok` set to `true` means only that the request was accepted; whether the funds are remitted is determined by the withdrawal record status.

Preconditions: a usable card has been selected through `GET /v3/portfolio/withdraw/cards`, and “Get withdrawal pre-check information” (`GET /v3/portfolio/withdraw/pre` or `GET /v4/portfolio/withdraw/pre`) has confirmed that the amount does not exceed `max_amount` and is not below the currency’s minimum withdrawal amount. If the card requires a payee address, save it first with `POST /v1/portfolio/withdraw/card/address`.

Side effects: creates a withdrawal request. On success, use the returned `id` to call `GET /v7/portfolio/withdraw/detail`, and find the request in `GET /v6/portfolio/withdraw/record`. While the status is `0` or `15`, it can be cancelled with `POST /v2/portfolio/withdraw/cancel`. On failure, handle the business code; for other codes, show `message` to the Client instead of resubmitting immediately.

When calling through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

A complete withdrawal flow runs in this order: get the withdrawal bank cards (`GET /v3/portfolio/withdraw/cards`) → get the withdrawal pre-check information and withdrawable amount (`GET /v3/portfolio/withdraw/pre`; some tenant channels use `GET /v4/portfolio/withdraw/pre`; to get only the withdrawable balance by currency, call `GET /v1/rms_gateway/get_account_all_single_currency_withdraw`) → check and add the payee address when required → submit the withdrawal request (`POST /v5/portfolio/withdraw`) → query withdrawal records and details → cancel the withdrawal or change the receiving bank card when needed.

MMF advance mode, with the same meaning as `is_pad_funded` in the pre-check:
- `1` - No redemption; the platform advances the funds
- `2` - Redeem the MMF before withdrawing

The Broker App currently always passes `2`.

Pagination: `page` starts at `1`; when `list` contains fewer items than `size`, there is no more data. Some tenant channels use `GET /v6/portfolio/withdraw/record/no/trade/auth`, a version that returns the same data without trading password verification and takes the same parameters.

Queries one withdrawal by withdrawal request id, including the amount, fee, status, order number, creation and update times, payee and receiving bank information, payee address, remarks, the history of receiving card changes, whether the receiving card can be changed, and any card change awaiting confirmation. Used on the withdrawal result and details pages.

Next steps: when `state` is `0` or `15`, cancel with `POST /v2/portfolio/withdraw/cancel` using `order_id`. When `can_edit_card` is `true`, change the receiving card with `PUT /v1/portfolio/withdraw/member/change/card`. When `to_be_changed_card` is returned, call `POST /v1/portfolio/withdraw/card/change/process` after the Client confirms, to accept the card change. Some tenant channels use `GET /v7/portfolio/withdraw/detail/no/trade/auth`, a version that returns the same data without trading password verification and takes the same parameter, but does not return `card_id`, `payee_address`, or `to_be_changed_card.card_id`.

When calling through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

Lets the Client replace the receiving bank card of a withdrawal request in progress. Used for the “Update Bank Info” action on the withdrawal details page. On success, the receiving bank information in the details is updated and a new entry is added to `records`.

Preconditions: `can_edit_card` in the withdrawal details is `true` and `state` is `0` or `15`. Pick the new card from `GET /v3/portfolio/withdraw/cards`; it must be verified (`status` is `2`), have a deposit witness status of `1` or `3`, have an `account_type` that matches the withdrawal currency or is `ALL`, and differ from the current receiving card. Before calling, call `POST /v1/portfolio/withdraw/card/addresscheck` with the new card; when `address_needed` is `true`, save the payee address with `POST /v1/portfolio/withdraw/card/address` first.

On success, query the details again. If the details contain a card change suggested by the review (`to_be_changed_card`), use `POST /v1/portfolio/withdraw/card/change/process` instead.

Before calling, call `POST /v1/portfolio/withdraw/card/addresscheck` with `to_be_changed_card.card_id`; when `address_needed` is `true`, save the payee address with `POST /v1/portfolio/withdraw/card/address` first. On success, query the details again. When the Client picks a new card themselves, use `PUT /v1/portfolio/withdraw/member/change/card` instead.

When `address_needed` is `true`, render the address form from `want_fields` and save it with `POST /v1/portfolio/withdraw/card/address`. When `address_valid` is `false`, the address must be completed or corrected before the withdrawal can continue.
